name: Alabama
agency: Alabama Law Enforcement Agency (ALEA), Driver License Division
permitAge: 15 (Stage I learner license; valid 4 years, renewable once; manual p. 9)

teen.supervisedHours: 50 hours of behind-the-wheel practice certified by a parent, legal guardian, grandparent or driving instructor, or an approved driver education course instead (Code of Ala. 32-6-7.2(b); ALEA GDL page). The manual does not give the hours.
teen.nightLimit: Stage II: no driving midnight-6 a.m. unless with parent/guardian or licensed driver 21+; exceptions for work, school-sponsored and religious events, medical/fire/police emergencies, hunting/fishing with a license (32-6-7.2(c))
teen.passengerLimit: Stage II: no more than one passenger besides parents, legal guardians, family members or a licensed driver 21+ (32-6-7.2(c)(2))
teen.phone: Stage II: no handheld communication device (32-6-7.2(c)(3)). All drivers: texting ban (32-5A-350; manual p. 32); hands-free law effective June 2024 (32-5A-350.1, Act 2023-478): holding a device is a violation when the driver is also seen swerving, changing lanes without a signal or otherwise driving improperly (manual p. 16)

notes: Handbook: ALEA Alabama Driver Manual, cover dated November 2024 (PDF created 2024-12-05, modified 2025-01-23); printed page = PDF page - 2. No official Spanish manual.
Knowledge test fee $5; the manual and ALEA site do not state the number of questions or the pass mark (third-party sites say 30 questions / 24 correct, not confirmed officially).
Written test offered in Arabic, Chinese, Farsi, French, German, Japanese, Korean, Russian, Spanish, Thai and Vietnamese, plus oral (audio) tests (manual p. 9).
Stage I: 15-year-old drives with a licensed driver 21+ or licensed/certified instructor beside (ALEA GDL page adds parent/guardian); after 16 any licensed driver (manual p. 9-10).
Stage III (unrestricted) at 17 after 6 months on Stage II; GDL violations extend restrictions 6 months or to age 18 (32-6-7.2(d)).

Speed (manual p. 60; 32-5A-171): urban district 30; unpaved 35; county paved 45; other 55; other 4+ lane highways 65; interstate 70. Note: ALEA speed-limits web page lists 25 mph residential, not in the statute.
Left-lane law (32-5A-80(d), Act 2019-515): may not stay in the leftmost interstate lane more than 1.5 miles without completely passing. Not in the manual.

Move Over (manual p. 68; 32-5A-58.2 as amended by Act 2024-295): vacate lane next to stopped emergency vehicle/wrecker (statute adds utility, road work/survey, garbage/recycling vehicles); if not possible slow at least 15 mph under limit; two-lane road with limit 20 or less: 10 mph.
School bus (manual p. 61): stop both ways on 4-6 lane undivided highway; no stop for bus on opposing roadway of a divided highway with 4+ lanes; stop at least 20 feet away (p. 62).
Right (and one-way to one-way left) turn on red after a full stop unless a sign prohibits it (manual p. 60-61).
Headlights required when wipers are used for rain, sleet or snow; intermittent wipers excluded (manual p. 71).
